title: Harder homework where a student fails: two curriculum rounds pass their gate on dev, and a fresh draw shows the gain is mostly the dev rows' own
request: Phase 7 (the owner): a student behind every choice; 29.12 tells the generators which kinds of table a student gets wrong on dev and makes more of those, the sealed sets untouched.
plan: Choose the point: room to learn on dev, errors a generator knob controls.
Each round: the kinds the student fails on dev, more tables of them in train groups only, the student fitted again as the generation's were.
Prove the parent's dev rows and sealed file unchanged, and record each round in the register's history.

decisions.why: split.strategy's errors come from two scenarios its state cannot tell apart (its ceiling is about the student's score): more tables of them cannot help; task.framing's errors sit in two kinds one knob controls.

decisions.decision: The failing kinds are taught together, in equal numbers.
decisions.why: Two kinds confused in shared states: teaching only one shifts the student's default answer and costs the other.

decisions.decision: New tables only in groups the datasets' hash puts in train, the parent's files checked by their bytes.
decisions.why: A new table must never reach dev or sealed, and the sealed file is never opened.

decisions.decision: The curriculum's student is not adopted.
decisions.why: Its dev gain was measured on the rows that also chose the kinds; on fresh tables it is +0.006 with an interval touching zero, below the gate's own margin.

change: dclab_core.benchgen2.task_table(kind=) (0.86.0); dclab_rnd/curriculum.py: errors by kind, new rows, rounds, the gate, publish, a register line per round, the fresh check; evidence/campaigns/curriculum_v1 (CUR-001 the gated run, CUR-002 and CUR-003 the fresh checks); the rounds' manifests and cards; the register's history no longer calls a return to an earlier student a slip.

findings.defect: The curriculum's dev gain did not hold on fresh tables.
findings.scenario: CUR-001: dev 0.9156 to 0.9362; a fresh draw of 600 tables: 0.9433 to 0.9392.
findings.cause: The rounds chose their kinds from the dev errors and were scored on the same dev rows.
findings.fix: Independent checks on fresh tables, reported beside the gate; the student not adopted.
findings.impact: An unexamined student would have been registered as the point's on a dev-specific gain.

findings.defect: The central claim needed a fresh check with an interval.
findings.scenario: On 2,000 fresh tables: +0.0057, 95% 0.000 to 0.012; the second round added 0.000 on dev.
findings.cause: Dev both chose the kinds and measured the gain; no arm of random-kind tables.
findings.fix: fresh_check: 2,000 tables of seeds no set uses, a paired bootstrap over tables (CUR-003); the status says what was and was not shown.

findings.defect: The round lines in the register carried an exam their students never sat.
findings.scenario: The rounds' lines showed exam false (the generation's failed exam); round 0's status said not examined though it sat the exam.
findings.cause: The line replaced the student but kept the verdict read for the registered one, and read the register without the workspace's ledger and routing.
findings.fix: Each line reads the workspace's ledger, routing and home; an exam is kept only where its version sat it, the status from the register's own rule.

findings.scenario: It names dclab-core's version, which moved.
findings.cause: make catalog not run after the version change.
findings.fix: The catalog rebuilt with make catalog.

findings.scenario: Only the generator, new rows and the kind reading had tests.
findings.fix: A whole run on a small parent with a quick student: one line per round, no round with an exam, the last round published, a changed sealed file never untouched.

findings.defect: The register tests had been loosened for the adopted student.
findings.scenario: Any examined point whose registered student differs from its exam passed silently.
findings.cause: An exception added while the curriculum's student was registered.
findings.fix: The student is not adopted: the tests are back as they were.

findings.defect: One kind's seeds could run into the next kind's.
findings.scenario: Above about 600 tables a kind, two tables of different kinds would share a group and a record id.
findings.cause: Each kind had a seed range of 1,000.
findings.fix: A run that would cross it is refused.

measurements.name: CUR-001, two rounds
measurements.gate: curriculum_gate_v1: round 2 at least 0.008 above round 0 on the parent's dev rows, no round more than 0.004 below the one before, the dev rows and sealed file byte-identical
measurements.against_gate: Round 2 at 0.9362 against round 0 at 0.9156 with 0.008 asked: met; no round below the one before; the parent's files unchanged.
limits: The rounds chose their kinds from the same dev rows.

measurements.name: CUR-003, a fresh draw
measurements.gate: none: an independent check after the verdict
limits: No arm of as many random-kind tables: targeted homework and more homework are not told apart.

outcome: The curriculum machinery works and the sealed sets stay untouched, but the honest result is that targeted homework lifted task.framing by little more than nothing on fresh tables: the student stays the generation's.
lessons: A set that chose what to teach cannot also be the set that judges it: keep a second draw for the verdict.
Before making more of what a student gets wrong, check whether the state can tell those cases apart at all.
risks: The register's history keeps the rounds' lines written before the fix with an exam they did not sit.
